title: Composition of sheaf inverse images on nested colimit generators
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be small sites and $v:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ functors for which precomposition takes sheaves of sets to sheaves of sets. Work in a fixed larger universe containing these sites. Let $\mathcal A$ be sets or abelian groups, and use the sheaf inverse images and adjunctions of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]. Thus $w_s\mathcal F=(w_p\mathcal F)^\#$, where $w_p\mathcal F(T)$ is the colimit of $\mathcal F(S)$ over the opposite of the category of pairs $(S,\alpha:T\to w(S))$; sheafification is [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For such a functor $w$ and a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on its source, denote by $\iota^w_{S,\alpha}:\mathcal F(S)\to(w_s\mathcal F)(T)$ the colimit coprojection followed by sheafification. The equality $(uv)^s=v^su^s$ of direct images determines a unique adjunction-compatible natural isomorphism
$$\kappa:u_sv_s\xrightarrow{\sim}(uv)_s.$$
Here adjunction compatibility means that $v^su^s(\kappa_{\mathcal F})\circ v^s(\eta^u_{v_s\mathcal F})\circ\eta^v_{\mathcal F}=\eta^{uv}_{\mathcal F}$, with $\eta^w$ the unit of $w_s\dashv w^s$. For every sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal C$ with values in $\mathcal A$, this comparison satisfies the following normalization: for $U\in\mathcal E$, $V\in\mathcal D$, $W\in\mathcal C$, arrows $\phi:U\to u(V)$ and $\psi:V\to v(W)$, and $x\in\mathcal F(W)$,
$$\kappa_{\mathcal F,U}\bigl(\iota^u_{V,\phi}(\iota^v_{W,\psi}(x))\bigr)=\iota^{uv}_{W,u(\psi)\phi}(x).$$
Moreover, for any sheaf $\mathcal H$ on $\mathcal E$, two sheaf morphisms $\alpha,\beta:u_sv_s\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$ are equal if their components have equal values on every element $\iota^u_{V,\phi}(\iota^v_{W,\psi}(x))$ with the indices above. For abelian sheaves this means equality on these generators, without assuming that every section is a single colimit representative. Both assertions are natural in $\mathcal F$ and in restrictions $U'\to U$.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites, adjunction-compatible comparison; generator normalization from the colimit adjunction construction in lemma-adjoints-u and lemma-adjoint-sheaves.

proof.text: For each of the functors $w=v,u,uv$, the hypothesis that precomposition preserves sheaves gives the direct-image functor $w^s$ on the indicated sheaf category. The defining presheaf formula gives $(uv)^s\mathcal H=\mathcal H\circ u\circ v=v^s(u^s\mathcal H)$, including the same equality on morphisms. The adjunction-and-sheafification construction of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] therefore supplies $w_s\dashv w^s$ and identifies $w_s\mathcal F$ with $(w_p\mathcal F)^\#$, with the colimit coprojections followed by the sheafification unit as the maps $\iota^w_{S,\alpha}$.

source.place: Tags 00VE and 00WX, construction of the presheaf left adjoint and its sheafification; Tag 03CB proof, equality $(u\circ v)^s=v^su^s$

proof.text: Compose the adjunctions $u_s\dashv u^s$ and $v_s\dashv v^s$ using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Its unit at $\mathcal F$ is $v^s(\eta^u_{v_s\mathcal F})\circ\eta^v_{\mathcal F}$. Since $(uv)^s=v^su^s$ by step 1, this is an adjunction for the same right adjoint as $(uv)_s\dashv(uv)^s$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with the identity right-adjoint isomorphism. It yields a unique natural isomorphism $\kappa:u_sv_s\xrightarrow{\sim}(uv)_s$ satisfying $v^su^s(\kappa_{\mathcal F})\circ v^s(\eta^u_{v_s\mathcal F})\circ\eta^v_{\mathcal F}=\eta^{uv}_{\mathcal F}$.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites; uniqueness of the compatible left-adjoint comparison, with Categories Tag 0B65

proof.text:
The unit equation from step 2 first gives the formula on the canonical
colimit generator: at $W\in\mathcal C$ and $x\in\mathcal F(W)$,
$\eta^v_{\mathcal F}$ uses the pair $(W,\mathrm{id}_{v(W)})$, and
$v^s(\eta^u)$ then uses $(v(W),\mathrm{id}_{u(v(W))})$; the composite unit
uses $(W,\mathrm{id}_{(uv)(W)})$. Thus $\kappa$ sends the identity-index
nested generator to the identity-index composite generator. For arbitrary
$\psi:V\to v(W)$ and $\phi:U\to u(V)$, the colimit coprojection maps
in the two successive colimits carry this identity-index generator to
$\iota^u_{V,\phi}(\iota^v_{W,\psi}(x))$; the corresponding map in the
single composite colimit carries it to
$\iota^{uv}_{W,u(\psi)\phi}(x)$. Naturality of the unit and of $\kappa$,
followed by the sheafification unit, therefore gives
$\kappa_{\mathcal F,U}(\iota^u_{V,\phi}(\iota^v_{W,\psi}(x)))=
\iota^{uv}_{W,u(\psi)\phi}(x)$. This uses only the defining
colimit coprojections and the universal sheafification map, so it does not
assume that an arbitrary sheafified section has a single colimit representative.

source.place: Tags 00VE and 00WX, unit on colimit coprojections; Tag 03CB, composition comparison

proof.text: Let $\alpha,\beta:u_sv_s\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$ have equal values on all the nested generators in the statement. Use the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], two maps out of $u_sv_s\mathcal F$ are equal once their adjuncts into $v^su^s\mathcal H$ are equal. The adjunct of either map is $v^su^s(\alpha)$, respectively $v^su^s(\beta)$, followed by the composite unit. On every section $x\in\mathcal F(W)$ of every object $W\in\mathcal C$, the composite unit is the nested generator from step 3, so the hypothesis makes these two adjuncts agree on every section; equality of natural transformations is componentwise. Thus $\alpha=\beta$. This argument applies to sets and to abelian groups and does not assert that every section of the sheafified source is itself a single colimit representative.

source.place: Tag 0B65, adjunct/counit uniqueness; combined with Sites Tag 03CB and the section formula from Tags 00VE and 00WX

proof.text: All constructions used above are functorial in $\mathcal F$ and in restriction maps $U'\to U$: the colimit coprojections, the sheafification unit, the two adjunction units, and the comparison supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] are natural. Therefore the normalization and the equality-detection assertion are natural in $\mathcal F$ and compatible with restrictions, as required.

source.place: Tags 00VE and 00WX, functoriality of the colimit adjunction and sheafification; Tag 03CB, naturality of the comparison

split_report.summary: Split the generic sheaf inverse-image composition lemma into five steps. The first establishes the direct-image equality and the three sheaf adjunctions; the second constructs the unique unit-compatible comparison by the composite-adjunction and conjugate-isomorphism lemmas; the third computes its value on nested colimit generators; the fourth proves that those generators detect equality by the composite adjunction; and the fifth records naturality in the sheaf and restrictions. No new DAG nodes were needed. Corrected step 3 to derive the arbitrary-generator formula from identity-index generators via the colimit coprojection maps and sheafification, rather than evaluating a unit equation on an element outside its domain.
split_report.blueprint: This realizes the nested-colimit composition comparison used in proof paragraph 4 of lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site: taking left adjoints, normalizing on nested generators, and detecting equality of the resulting sheaf maps.
